By
Adam Safdi
, WCI Columnist
On January 31, 2024, I received a call at 4am from a strange number. Normally, I keep my phone on vibrate overnight, but this number kept calling repeatedly. Eventually, I woke up and answered the phone. The caller said, “Adam? This is Adam, right? This is Jack, a friend of your dad. I’m sorry to call so early, but I have some distressing news.”
Jack went on to tell me that the police were taking my dad to the local hospital’s emergency department. Over the next few hours, we pieced together the story. My dad had wandered out of his house the night before, presumably to go for a walk. It started raining, and he became disoriented, unable to find his way home. He found a house with an unlocked door and went inside. He fell asleep in a spare bedroom. When he woke early the next morning, he became frustrated and confused by his unfamiliar surroundings.
The couple who lived there found him wandering in their kitchen. After the initial shock, they realized my dad posed no threat, but they called 911 due to the intrusion. No charges were filed, and the police recognized what our family had feared for some time: dementia. The local ER staff evaluated him for acute medical issues, and after finding nothing urgent, they sent him home.
I must first publicly express my gratitude to the couple who found my dad. I can only imagine how distressing it must have been to find a stranger in their home. I sent them a letter thanking them for their kindness and understanding.
Let me explain a little bit about my father’s situation. My mother passed away in 2018, and my father has lived alone since. He has a new girlfriend who lives 30 minutes away. My brother lives two hours away, and I live three time zones away. Up until that point, we knew he had some memory difficulties, and a local neurologist had diagnosed him with mild cognitive impairment.
But we didn’t think it was that severe.
There had been instances where my dad chose mismatched or inappropriate clothing, burned his toast, or replaced the telephone in the refrigerator instead of on the phone charger. However, after the January 2024 incident, we went back to his neurologist, who sadly confirmed that with my dad’s combination of cognitive and functional impairments—most notably his lack of direction, wandering, and getting lost—meant that he had progressed from mild cognitive impairment to dementia. It became clear that my dad was likely no longer safe to be by himself at home.
While my dad was the breadwinner during his working years, my mother managed the household finances. She and my father had bought
long-term care (LTC) insurance
policies for the possibility of prolonged illness later in life. As best as I can tell from the paperwork, my parents bought these policies in 2004, they each paid about $14,000 in annual premiums for 10 years, and the daily benefit started at $200 per day. I was unaware of these policies when my mother died (after a relatively short illness), but I became aware of them when an uncle called and mentioned, “Your father has a long-term care insurance policy. I helped him get it.”
Thus began the long process of filing and obtaining claims with the LTC insurance company. I’d like to share some lessons learned from this experience.
What to Do with Your Relative's Long-Term Care Insurance
#1 Call the Insurance Company to Obtain an Application to File a Claim
For a while, my brother and I tried to track down the actual policy. We sifted through stacks of paperwork at our dad’s house and became frustrated (fairly and unfairly) that he didn’t know where the papers were located. When we finally called the insurance company, it, of course, had his policy on file. The company sent us an application, and we began filling out the paperwork. The application included several parts:
Authorization to obtain and disclose information
Claimant’s statement
Attending physician’s statement
Benefit direct deposit form
Fraud notice
Try to get a point of contact in the company's call center if possible. We found calling more fruitful than emailing. Many of our emails went completely unanswered, which was a source of frustration and delayed the process.
More information here:
The Challenges of Long-Distance Eldercare
Cost of Caring for Aging Parents

data.title: At a Loss for Words: A flawed idea is teaching kids to be poor readers (2019)
data.author: Akronymus
data.article_summary: 《Sold a Story》播客探讨了美国阅读教学中的一个长期误区：一种被认知科学家数十年前就证明错误的理念，却仍在 schools 中广泛使用，导致许多学生无法有效学习阅读。主持人Emily Hanford调查了推广此错误理念的作家及其相关出版公司，揭示出教育界因相信错误理论而产生的后果，包括对孩子的伤害、资金的浪费及教育系统的动荡。播客还讨论了布什总统的“阅读优先”计划、著名教育家Lucy Calkins的影响、出版公司Heinemann的角色以及目前各界的反思与改革努力。最终，许多学区开始改变教学方法，转向基于科学研究的阅读教学。

Sold a Story: How Teaching Kids to Read Went So Wrong
There's an idea about how children learn to read that's held sway in schools for more than a generation — even though it was proven wrong by cognitive scientists decades ago. Teaching methods based on this idea can make it harder for children to learn how to read. In this podcast, host Emily Hanford investigates the influential authors who promote this idea and the company that sells their work. It's an exposé of how educators came to believe in something that isn't true and are now reckoning with the consequences — children harmed, money wasted, an education system upended.
▼
FOLLOW THE SHOW
▼

EPISODES
EPISODE 1
The Problem
Lee Gaul watches his daughter's lessons during Zoom school and discovers a dismaying truth: She can't read. Little Zoe isn't the only one. Sixty-five percent of fourth graders in the United States are not proficient readers. Kids need to learn specific skills to become good readers, and in many schools, those skills are not being taught.
TRANSCRIPT
|
DOWNLOAD

The Idea
Sixty years ago, Marie Clay developed a way to teach reading she said would help kids who were falling behind. They'd catch up and never need help again. Today, her program remains popular, and her theory about how people read is at the root of a lot of reading instruction in schools. But Marie Clay was wrong.

The Battle
President George W. Bush made improving reading instruction a priority. He got Congress to provide money to schools that used reading programs supported by scientific research. But backers of Marie Clay's ideas saw Bush's Reading First initiative as a threat.

The Superstar
Teachers sing songs about Lucy Calkins. The longtime professor at Columbia University's Teachers College is one of the most influential people in American elementary education today. Her admirers call her books "bibles." Why didn't she know that scientific research contradicted reading strategies she promoted?

44766962.article_summary: 《Sold a Story》播客探讨了美国阅读教学中的一个长期误区：一种被认知科学家数十年前就证明错误的理念，却仍在 schools 中广泛使用，导致许多学生无法有效学习阅读。主持人Emily Hanford调查了推广此错误理念的作家及其相关出版公司，揭示出教育界因相信错误理论而产生的后果，包括对孩子的伤害、资金的浪费及教育系统的动荡。播客还讨论了布什总统的“阅读优先”计划、著名教育家Lucy Calkins的影响、出版公司Heinemann的角色以及目前各界的反思与改革努力。最终，许多学区开始改变教学方法，转向基于科学研究的阅读教学。
44766962.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于儿童阅读教学方法的争议，特别是音素教学法（phonics）与整体语言法（whole word/context-based）的对比，以及对教师和教育系统的信任问题。

不同观点：
• **支持音素教学法**：
   - [hyperman1] 提到自己早期学习音符时被要求通过上下文猜测，而不是学习实际规则，导致对教师的不信任。他认为应该追求准确的规则，而不是依赖“感觉对”的上下文猜测。
   - [giardini] 强烈支持音素教学法，认为这是有效的阅读教学方法，并批评后来的“改进”方法扰乱了阅读教学。
   - [aDyslecticCrow] 作为一位有阅读障碍的人，认为音素教学法在学习外语单词时更有效，而猜测单词会造成学习障碍。
   - [SoftTalker] 回忆自己20世纪70年代的学习经历，表示当时通过字母和发音学习阅读，没有依赖“上下文”或“图片提示”。

• **支持上下文和整体语言法**：
   - [twotwotwo] 提到《Teach Your Child to Read in 100 Easy Lessons》这本书，认为通过循序渐进的方法可以让孩子学会阅读，并强调孩子通过上下文和单词识别可以找到阅读的捷径。
   - [bluesounddirect] 批评教育行业和教师更关注如何从服务中获利，而不是帮助孩子阅读，暗示某些教学方法可能被商业化利用。

• **对两种方法的批判与反思**：
   - [camgunz] 引用英国的例子，指出音素教学法在提升阅读能力方面并不总是有效，并提供了相关研究链接，认为音素法并非唯一解决方案。
   - [xg15] 通过实例质疑基于图形、句法或语义线索的阅读方法的局限性，指出这些方法在某些情况下会失败。

• **对教育系统的批评**：
   - [luckydata] 作为移民和家长，批评美国教育系统中教师使用的“半科学”方法，认为学生学习负担不足，家长的介入能带来更好的学习效果。
   - [andrewstuart] 强调为孩子提供适合年龄的现代书籍的重要性，通过兴趣驱动阅读。

补充讨论：
• ** dyslexia（阅读障碍）的影响**：
   - [aDyslecticCrow] 分享了自己作为阅读障碍者的学习经历，指出音素法在早期学习中对他造成了困难，但最终通过整体单词识别提高了阅读速度，并提出了对上下文猜测法的质疑。

• **对教育科学方法的质疑**：
   - [didibus] 对“观察科学”和“认知科学”的区别提出疑问，质疑某些教育方法是否基于严格的实验或双盲研究，还是仅仅依赖个人经验。

争议焦点：
• **音素教学法与整体语言法的优劣**：一方认为音素法提供了准确的规则和基础，另一方则认为上下文猜测和整体单词识别更符合实际阅读过程。

主要讨论点：SpaceX卫星发射及其影响，以及对卫星数据的获取和准确性的讨论

不同观点：
• NoPicklez对SpaceX发射大量卫星表示惊讶，并指出发射火箭的"自由度"——虽然需要 originating country 的批准，但无需其他国家的许可。
• carlsborg纠正有关卫星数量的过时信息，指出SpaceX已有超过7500颗卫星在轨，并在一年内增加了2300多颗。
• voigt提出是否存在类似于Flightradar24的卫星追踪网站，并讨论了实现"实时"卫星可视化的可能性和技术挑战。
• account-5对一篇销售宣传文章做出评论，指出其在文章中植入广告的巧妙方式。
• perihelions分享了一篇更新的长篇文章，讨论了SpaceX和中国在太空领域的竞争。
• mhio提供了一个由Jonathan McDowell维护的卫星数据目录（GCAT），并提醒使用者注意数据日期格式的问题。
• storgaard指出GEO, LEO, MEO, HEO中"E"代表的不同含义，提供了一些技术背景。
• keyle和theyinwhy都认为2021年的数据在快速变化的太空领域已经不再相关，特别是考虑到SpaceX快速增加卫星数量。
• KurSix感叹单个私营公司拥有超过三分之一的地球轨道卫星，过去太空似乎是政府和科幻的领域。
• AndroTux质疑欧盟是否几乎没有军用卫星，提到法国CNES可能有少量卫星。
• fireflymetavrse指出仅根据卫星数量统计可能具有误导性，因为没有区分不同类型和重量的卫星。
• elephant81怀疑有一些未列出的美国NRO卫星，提到Misty等隐形卫星。
• pulvinar指出Dewesoft的卫星统计可能不准确，特别是对非前50名拥有者的统计，并举例奥地利的卫星数量错误。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到数据准确性和及时性的问题，特别是对SpaceX快速增加卫星数量的动态变化。
• 有对私营公司（如SpaceX）在太空领域主导地位的讨论，以及对政府和军用卫星的关注。
• 技术上，有对实时卫星追踪和数据可视化的兴趣和讨论，涉及到数据获取和计算的技术挑战。
• 对卫星统计方法的批评，指出数量统计可能忽略了卫星类型和重量的差异。

data.title: Corporation for Public Broadcasting ceasing operations
data.author: coloneltcb
data.article_summary: 2025年8月1日，美国公共广播公司（CPB）宣布将有序关闭运营，因联邦拨款被取消。这是CPB成立近60年来首次失去联邦资金。CPB一直通过与地方台和制作人合作，支持教育内容、地方新闻、紧急通讯、文化节目等。尽管公众努力呼吁保留资助，CPB仍将关闭大部分员工职位，仅留一小团队处理后续事务至2026年1月。CPB总裁Patricia Harrison表示，将确保关闭过程透明、负责，并继续支持合作伙伴。CPB董事会正处理关闭相关的法律、财务和运营问题，并将定期更新情况。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：公共广播公司（CPB）及其资助的公共广播电视（PBS）和全国公共广播电台（NPR）的资金、内容制作、政治争议及其社会影响。

不同观点：
• **CPB的角色与影响**：[tptacek] 指出CPB主要是一个拨款管理机构，并不直接制作PBS节目，PBS节目通常由私人制作并由地方电视台购买。因此，CPB的关闭不意味着PBS节目的终结，而是资金分配机制的改变。[atonse] 补充CPB只占PBS资金的15%，大部分资金来自捐赠，因此CPB的关闭不会直接导致PBS的消亡。

• **政治与意识形态争议**：[smithkl42] 认为NPR近年来表现出左倾偏见，且缺乏自我反省，类似于右翼的Fox新闻。相反，[legitster] 认为PBS和NPR是相对无偏见的新闻来源，尤其在儿童节目方面表现出色，且无广告和收费，非常珍贵。[delichon] 则从自由主义角度反对政府资助媒体，认为这是对言论自由的侵犯。

• **情感与历史价值**：[buildmonkey] 表达了对CPB资助的经典节目如《罗杰斯先生的左邻右舍》和《芝麻街》的怀念，认为其消失是文化的损失。[kianN] 强调了PBS儿童节目对其成长的积极影响，认为这种投资无法立即衡量但非常重要。

• **未来的解决方案与建议**：[munchler] 认为公共广播可能会在没有政治干预的情况下变得更强大，虽然短期内会经历痛苦。[qrush] 呼吁个人直接捐款支持地方公共媒体站。[abeppu] 提出将联邦政府提供的服务分解，允许各州自行决定是否继续资助公共广播。[falaki] 建议所有政府项目应设有有效期。

补充讨论：
• **资金与捐赠机制的复杂性**：[wkoszek] 对如何有效捐款支持PBS和地方电视台感到困惑，表明公众对捐赠机制的理解存在困难。[bbanyc] 指出NPR的偏见和听众流失问题，但认为完全取消资助是过度反应，会导致优质节目减少和地方台关闭。

争议的焦点：
• 公共广播是否应该由政府资助，以及这种资助是否侵犯了言论自由。
• PBS和NPR是否存在明显的政治偏见，以及这种偏见是否影响了其公信力。
• CPB的关闭对公共广播内容的实际影响究竟有多大。

整体来看，讨论围绕公共广播的资金来源、政治影响及其社会文化价值展开，各方对CPB关闭的看法各异，反映了不同政治立场和个人经历对这一问题的复杂影响。

44759382.article_content:
Skip to main content
Corporation for Public Broadcasting Addresses Operations Following Loss of Federal Funding
Print
August 1, 2025
WASHINGTON, D.C.
(August 1, 2025) – The Corporation for Public Broadcasting (CPB) announced today that it will begin an orderly wind-down of its operations following the passage of a federal rescissions package and the release of the Senate Appropriations Committee’s FY 2026 Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies (Labor-H) appropriations bill, which excludes funding for CPB for the first time in more than five decades.
For nearly 60 years, CPB has carried out its Congressional mission to build and sustain a trusted public media system that informs, educates, and serves communities across the country. Through partnerships with local stations and producers, CPB has supported educational content, locally relevant journalism, emergency communications, cultural programming, and essential services for Americans in every community.
“Despite the extraordinary efforts of millions of Americans who called, wrote, and petitioned Congress to preserve federal funding for CPB, we now face the difficult reality of closing our operations,” said CPB President and CEO Patricia Harrison. “CPB remains committed to fulfilling its fiduciary responsibilities and supporting our partners through this transition with transparency and care.”
CPB informed its employees today that the majority of staff positions will conclude with the close of the fiscal year on September 30, 2025. A small transition team will remain through January 2026 to ensure a responsible and orderly closeout of operations. This team will focus on compliance, final distributions, and resolution of long-term financial obligations, including ensuring continuity for music rights and royalties that remain essential to the public media system.
“Public media has been one of the most trusted institutions in American life, providing educational opportunity, emergency alerts, civil discourse, and cultural connection to every corner of the country,” Harrison said. “We are deeply grateful to our partners across the system for their resilience, leadership, and unwavering dedication to serving the American people.”
CPB’s Board of Directors and management are working closely to address the legal, financial, and operational requirements of the closure. CPB will provide regular updates and guidance to stations and producers navigating the profound challenges ahead.
About CPB
The Corporation for Public Broadcasting (CPB), a private, nonprofit corporation authorized by Congress in 1967, is the steward of the federal government's investment in public broadcasting. It helps support the operations of more than 1,500 locally managed and operated public television and radio stations nationwide. CPB is also the largest single source of funding for research, technology, and program development for public radio, television, and related online services. For more information, visit
www.cpb.org
and follow us on

, and

for email updates.

主要讨论点：城市交通安全与规划，特别是在不同国家和地区的比较，以及如何通过城市设计、政策和文化来提高交通安全。

不同观点：
• PaulRobinson：描述了在赫尔辛基遇到的情况，赞扬了当地对安全的高标准， contractors在午夜作业时未设置路障，他的芬兰同事立即报警处理，显示出对安全的高度重视。Paul认为这种严格执行安全标准是赫尔辛基交通较为安全的原因。
• kqr：提出一个疑问，即很多关于如何减少交通死亡的措施（如减速、儿童安全座椅等）并不昂贵，但为何很多地方没有实施。他对全球各地交通安全标准的不一致表示困惑。
• tlogan：认为赫尔辛基的交通安全优势可能并不在于城市规划的特殊性，而仅仅是因为车辆较少。他指出赫尔辛基人均车辆拥有量远低于美国城市，因此交通事故发生率低。他还提到一些美国城市也有零交通事故死亡的例子。
• tsoukase：强调驾驶是一项极端责任，车辆高速行驶时很容易导致事故，尤其是速度过快时。他认为各国政府应采取严厉措施减少车祸，特别是在那些经常发生致命事故的角落和区域。
• hmottestad：描述了奥斯陆在处理卡车相关交通事故中的问题，尤其是卡车司机的责任和法庭处理上的争议。他指出卡车在城市中造成的安全隐患，并期待更严格的监管。
• knolan：批评了爱尔兰在交通安全上的执法不力，指出警力不足、道路安全管理机构无能等问题。他还提到爱尔兰司机普遍不尊重行人和骑行者，经常非法停车甚至在人行道上驾驶。

补充讨论：
• iambateman 和 Tiktaalik 强调了安全改进的隐性好处，比如那些因为改进措施而没有发生的事故往往不被注意。
• max_ 和 swader999 认为赫尔辛基的成功在于30公里/小时的限速、狭窄的街道和安全意识强的文化。
• matsemann 支持通过改变卡车设计来提高城市交通安全，建议城市中的卡车应像公交车一样设计，以提高视野和安全性。
• johnklos 赞扬了赫尔辛基的公共交通系统，认为其高效和便捷使得城市交通更加安全和顺畅。
• pentagrama 推荐了YouTube频道 "Not Just Bikes" 来讨论城市交通和移动性问题。

争议焦点：
• 不同城市和国家在交通安全执行上的差异，尤其是在赫尔辛基等城市的安全措施是否能广泛应用于其他地方。
• 爱尔兰交通安全执法不力和司机不尊重行人的问题与其他地区如赫尔辛基或奥斯陆的对比。
• 关于卡车在城市中造成安全隐患的责任归属问题，特别是在奥斯陆的案例中法院的判决争议。

data.title: I tried living on IPv6 for a day
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者尝试仅使用IPv6协议上网的实验经历。尽管IPv6在25年前就被标准化，但其普及速度很慢，大多数系统仍然同时运行IPv4和IPv6。作者想测试是否可以完全依赖IPv6进行日常使用，结果发现许多常用服务无法正常工作，例如XDA的CMS和Slack，而Gmail等部分服务则表现良好。作者的智能手机由于运营商的设置，也依赖于IPv4到IPv6的转换技术。实验表明，尽管IPv6已经推出多年，但要完全摆脱IPv4仍面临许多挑战，尤其在工作相关应用和VPN连接方面。最终，作者无法完成工作，但有时间浏览Facebook。这凸显了IPv6普及过程中的现实困难。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：IPv4与IPv6的现状、优缺点、过渡挑战及应用情况

不同观点：
• **IPv4不会很快消失**：apitman认为，除非大规模采用p2p协议，否则IPv4不会很快被取代。NAT和SNI已经解决了大部分问题，维持现状对大型组织有利，因此IPv6的普及面临阻力。
• **实际使用中的问题**：kacesensitive分享了自己在使用IPv4时遇到的DNS问题，并提到在更换设备后问题才得以解决。这表明在实际应用中，用户仍可能遇到各种问题。
• **IPv6的支持和配置**：throw0101d和herczegzsolt指出，已经有ISP和一些工具支持IPv6，并分享了具体配置方法。然而，herczegzsolt也提到，尽管IPv6有优点，但动态前缀等问题依然存在。
• **消费者对IPv6的接受度**：ectospheno认为，只有当主流消费电子产品（如PlayStation和Nintendo）支持IPv6时，消费者才会真正关心IPv6的普及。
• **IPv4地址稀缺的“好处”**：redox99认为，IPv4地址稀缺在一定程度上可以帮助限制DDoS攻击，具有一定的安全优势。
• **IPv6的增长趋势**：easterncalculus提到，Google的IPv6流量已经接近50%，显示出IPv6的增长趋势。
• **部署中的挑战**：sybercecurity指出，在新项目中部署IPv6较为容易，但在有遗留IPv4系统的环境中则可能变得复杂。
• **Apple的IPv6推动作用**：evaXhill赞扬Apple对IPv6的支持，认为这对推动IPv6的普及起到了积极作用。
• **IPv4到IPv6过渡的实际困难**：WarOnPrivacy和PaulKeeble分享了他们在关闭IPv4或切换到IPv6时遇到的实际困难，包括技术问题和服务不稳定。
• **IPv6在家庭网络中的问题**：dogcow指出，ISP分配的前缀不稳定和单一子网限制是家庭用户迁移到IPv6的主要障碍。

补充讨论：
• **IPv6的优势和NAT的作用**：ghusto提问，如果不希望直接路由而依赖NAT，IPv6的优势是什么？这反映了部分用户对NAT作为一种功能而非缺陷的看法。
• **IPv6-only服务器的可访问性**：IshKebab提出一个有趣的问题，即能够连接到IPv6-only服务器的用户比例是多少，这涉及到IPv6的实际普及程度。

争议焦点：
• **IPv4和IPv6的过渡时间**：一方认为IPv4会长期存在，另一方认为IPv6正在快速增长并最终会取代IPv4。
• **NAT的角色**：一些用户认为NAT是一个有用的功能，而另一些用户则认为IPv6的无NAT环境是其优势之一。

总结：讨论围绕IPv4与IPv6的现状、各自的优缺点以及过渡过程中面临的实际挑战展开。不同的技术背景和使用场景导致了对这两种协议的不同看法和争议。

Generate a summary of this story
Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents:
Here is a simplified version of the story contents:
Here is a lighthearted take on the story contents:
Explore a different perspective:
Show me the facts
Explain it like I’m 5
Give me a lighthearted recap
It's been a quarter of a century since the first
IPv6 standard
was finalized as RFC 2460, and to say adoption has been slow is an understatement. The pool of available
IPv4
addresses has been exhausted for quite a while now, and in fact, was
running out for public use
years ago. Yet it's still not gone, with most systems that have adopted IPv6 running a dual-stack configuration that also includes IPv4.
I wondered if you could survive on just IPv6. Surely, it's an established enough protocol that it would work for daily use. Oh, dear reader, if it were only so. The things I rely on daily to
actually do work
did not want to cooperate at all
. Well, there was one exception—a big shout-out to Gmail for supporting modern internet protocols. On the other hand, the things that try to distract me during the workday all worked flawlessly.
Oh, and my smartphone worked for everything, but that's down to
Apple requiring App Store developers to support IPv6-only networks
and a bunch of networking shenanigans on the back end of cellular connectivity. This whole experiment felt deeply ironic, as my cellular provider and ISP both use IPv6 on the back end for routing, but getting that to translate to a usable internet experience was a chore.
Time to turn off IPv4
This was harder than I expected it would be
The thing about trying to turn off an internet protocol that's been established for decades is, well, it's bloody everywhere. Some hardware has IPv4-only network stacks, and while the major operating systems all support IPv6, not every program they rely on does. But that's part of the point of this experiment. The tech world has had decades to adapt to IPv6, and I wanted to see how they'd handled things.
I'd put together the basic parts of a plan. I'd use
an OPNsense router
and remove the IPv4 address from the interface so it could only use IPv6. I also removed IPv4 from the network adapter on the laptop I'd be using that day, so it only had IPv6 routing, and confirmed that it worked. The only thing I use daily that I couldn't remove IPv4 from completely was my smartphone because while my network carrier uses IPv6, it also uses 464XLAT. This would be no good for our test, as 464XLAT uses stateless translation from customer-side translators (CLAT) and stateful translation on the provider-side (PLAT).. That design keeps an IPv4 software stack on the phone for legacy apps, but every packet on the air-link is pure IPv6. Outbound IPv4 traffic is translated to IPv6 by the CLAT, crosses the network as IPv6, and is converted back to IPv4 by the carrier's NAT64 just before it hits the legacy internet. In other words, the transport path is all IPv6, yet the handset still carries an IPv4 stack, so using it would kind of undermine the entire purpose of an IPv6-only experiment.
Thankfully, Verizon FiOS rolled out IPv6 support to my area a while ago; otherwise, this whole thing would have ended here. It's also a minor blessing that they slowed the 2 Gig rollout; otherwise, I'd have no IPv6 because it's not enabled on the highest tier in my region, which I assume is for troubleshooting purposes. I do have a T-Mobile 5G router that is IPv6-only, but that's also subject to 464XLAT translation like my cell phone and would derail everything because I have no control over the translation to IPv4. In other words, everything would work as usual. Even after all of that, you'll need something like DNS64 to resolve IPv4-only hostnames. Any service without an AAAA DNS record (a DNS A record specifically for an IPv6 address) won't load on an IPv6-only network.
It went about as well as I expected, really
I couldn't do my job, but that meant I had plenty of time to browse Facebook
Close
The stage was set for trying to survive with an IPv6-only network and connection to the Internet. I couldn't quite turn everything IPv4 off because I'm not the only person using the Internet in the house, but segregating some devices with an IPv6-only router was the next best thing. I had some thoughts about what would likely work and what wouldn't, but I wasn't sure if I'd be able to get any work done, let alone my usual workflow.
As it turned out, I couldn't. XDA's CMS wouldn't load on the IPv6-only connection. Neither would Slack, but I was granted some reprieve by Gmail, and the rest of Google Workplace happily connected. I couldn't upload any work to the site, but at least I could write in Google Docs for later use. I also couldn't connect to Proton VPN, and after a bit of searching, I found the reason: while traffic will go through the tunnel as IPv6, it needs IPv4 to make the initial connection. You can edit the WireGuard profile ProtonVPN uses to allow for it, but by default,

data.title: 6 Weeks of Claude Code
data.author: mike1o1
data.article_summary: 本文作者回顾了使用Claude Code辅助编程的短短六周内，自己的工作效率和方式发生的巨大变化。Claude Code让他不再需要逐行编写代码，而是可以快速生成整体框架，再通过代码审查和编辑进行调整。这种新方式让他在完成日常工作的同时，独自解决了许多技术债务问题，例如将React Native组件转换为React、迁移数据库模型、改写iOS启动系统等。这些任务以往可能需要数周甚至更长时间，而现在可以在后台快速完成。作者认为，这种变革类似于摄影技术对绘画的影响，编程的定义正在发生根本变化。尽管LLMs（大语言模型）可能带来社会问题，但其对编程的变革已不可逆转。作者还分享了“先尝试后决策”的新习惯，强调在做出最终判断前先动手试验。总的来说，Claude Code极大地提高了工作效率，改变了作者对技术债务和创新的处理方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Claude Code的使用体验、优缺点以及对开发者的影响

不同观点：
• [积极观点 - lukaslalinsky, arrowsmith, buffer1337, jeswin, lysecret, blackqueeriroh, softwaredoug]  
这些用户普遍对Claude Code持积极态度。他们认为Claude Code能够显著提升开发效率，尤其是在代码生成、项目管理和自动化任务方面。lukaslalinsky强调了其学习曲线和需要编程基础，但表示在熟悉后非常有用，甚至考虑升级到更高级的付费计划。arrowsmith扩展了Claude的能力，指出它不仅能写代码，还能控制整个计算机，执行诸如裁剪图片、提取音频等任务。buffer1337分享了使用技巧，如选择合适的初始设置和有效使用第一提示。jeswin和lysecret则强调了AI辅助下的测试驱动开发和代码质量提升。blackqueeriroh特别提到工具对个人学习与成长的帮助，尤其是在时间有限和注意力分散的情况下。

• [消极观点 - acedTrex, lbrito, floppyd]  
这些用户对Claude Code持较为消极或保留态度。acedTrex表示经常遇到错误和速度慢的问题，认为其在节省精神能量方面并不理想。lbrito对依赖这些工具创造的未来世界表示反感，尽管他自己也在使用。floppyd则关心Gemini CLI的免费替代方案，认为对于业余编码者来说，付费使用Claude Code并不值得。

44746621.article_content:
It is wild to think that it has been only a handful of weeks.
Claude Code has considerably changed my relationship to writing and maintaining code at scale. I still write code at the same level of quality, but I feel like I have a new freedom of expression which is hard to fully articulate.
Claude Code has decoupled myself from writing every line of code, I still consider myself fully responsible for everything I ship to Puzzmo, but the ability to instantly create a whole scene instead of going line by line, word by word is incredibly powerful.
I believe with Claude Code, we are at the
“introduction of photography”
period of programming. Painting by hand just doesn’t have the same appeal anymore when a single concept can just appear and you shape it into the thing you want with your code review and editing skills.
If this feels like an intimidating line-of-thought then welcome to the mid-2020s, nothing is stable anymore and change is the only constant. Sorry. I didn’t make it so nearly all of culture’s changes are
bad
, and I think that LLMs are already doing social damage and will do much worse in the future - but this genie is fully out of the bottle and it is substantially going to change what we think of as programming.
A Retrospective on the last 6 Weeks
#
This article builds on
“On Coding with Claude”
which I wrote after using Claude for a week. If you think that I am AI-pilled, you can get my nuanced take on LLMs at
the start
of that post.
That said, this is transformative and I want to try give you some perspective from the last 6 weeks of activity in the Puzzmo engineering space to try and show you what I’ve been seeing.
Maintenance is Significantly Cheaper
#
I have been on many projects with people which have taken weeks full-time to perform some sort of mundane task: “converting this JS codebase to TypeScript”, “Update to Swift X”, “Switch to a monorepo” they’re the kind of things which are delicate migrations which require a gazillion rebases.
Here is a list of things which I have completed,
solo
, since getting access to Claude Code:
Converting hundreds of React Native components to just React
Replaced 3 non-trivial RedwoodJS systems with home-grown or mature, supported replacements
Built complex REPLs for multiple internal and external projects
Switched almost every db model to have a consistent ‘flags’ system for booleans
Converted from Jest to Vitest
Created our front-end testing strategies for React
Moved many things defined in code to run via the CMS
Made significant headway on server-side rendering
Re-wrote the iOS app’s launch system due to deprecations
Built a suite of LLM created (and framed as such, hen hand annotated) documentation for systems like leaderboards, dailies etc
Converted a significant amount of our design system primitives to use base-ui
Migrated significant code from inline styles to stylex
Converted all animations in puzzmo.com to use the same techniques as games
Fixed multiple bugs which have been around since the start of Puzzmo
Updated all Vite integrations
Migrate all Puzzmo production projects to node 22
Convert the games repo to a real monorepo
Built iPad support for the Puzzmo app
None of these projects are the “actual work” which I need to do on a day to day basis as the ‘bizdev’ guy on Puzzmo for this year. These are
literally side-projects
which I did
on my own
while working on something else.
For clarity in the back because this is shocking to me, while I was still working on the existing roadmap I had prior to Claude Code over the last 6 weeks, I accomplished all of these things on my own. Mostly in the background (and then with a polish pass day for some of the larger ones). I didn’t go from working ~10 hour days to working ~16 hours or anything like that either.
This was years of
“tech debt” / “tech innovation”
backlog for me! Done in just over a month and a half.
If you understand what you are doing, the capacity for building and handling the breadth of tasks which typically live within the remit of “technical debt”
do not need to be treated as debt
and you can just do it as you are working on other things.
‘carving out some time on the schedule’
is now so incredibly cheap that getting started and making a serious dint is
something you can prime before going into a meeting
, then deciding if you thought it was the right thing after. Mind-blowing.
Write First, Decide Later
#
A habit I have been trying to form is to give an idea a shot before I fully shoot it down. For example, since day 1 on Puzzmo I had been waiting on figuring out a testing strategy for the front-end because I wanted to be able to hire someone to fully own “puzzmo.com” and a part of that is figuring out how to not do as many regressions as we get.
Figuring out a testing strategy for the front-end isn’t pretty, and I have seen a lot of really bad test suites which over-test and become brittle things that engineers don’t like to work with. The mix of networking, react, the scope of contex

data.title: Modeling Open-World Cognition as On-Demand Synthesis of Probabilistic Models
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种名为“模型合成架构”（MSA）的计算模型，用于模拟人类在开放世界中的认知能力。该架构结合了分布式和符号化表示，利用语言模型实现基于全局相关性的信息检索和模型合成，并通过概率程序构建量身定制的心理模型。研究通过一个体育场景数据集测试了MSA在 novel 因果推理中的表现，结果显示MSA在模拟人类判断方面优于仅基于语言模型的方法。这表明MSA能够更好地实现局部连贯推理，为理解和复制人类在开放领域中的推理能力提供了新路径。本文在CogSci 2025会议上发表。

View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
When faced with novel situations, people are able to marshal relevant considerations from a wide range of background knowledge and put these to use in inferences and predictions. What permits us to draw in globally relevant information and reason over it coherently? Here, we explore the hypothesis that people use a combination of distributed and symbolic representations to construct bespoke mental models tailored to novel situations. We propose a computational implementation of this idea -- a ``Model Synthesis Architecture'' (MSA) -- using language models to implement global relevance-based retrieval and model synthesis and probabilistic programs to implement bespoke, coherent world models. We evaluate our MSA as a model of human judgments on a novel reasoning dataset. The dataset -- built around a `Model Olympics` domain of sports vignettes -- tests models' capacity for human-like, open-ended reasoning by requiring (i) judgments about novel causal structures described in language; (ii) drawing on large bodies of background knowledge; and (iii) doing both in light of observations that introduce arbitrary novel variables. Our MSA approach captures human judgments better than language model-only baselines, under both direct and chain-of-thought generations from the LM that supports model synthesis. These results suggest that MSAs can be implemented in a way that mirrors people's ability to deliver locally coherent reasoning over globally relevant variables, offering a path to understanding and replicating human reasoning in open-ended domains.

data.title: Helion begins work on Washington nuclear fusion plant
data.author: mpweiher
data.article_summary: Helion，一家获得微软支持的核聚变公司，已在华盛顿州奇兰县开始建设其首个核聚变发电厂——Orion。该电厂计划于2028年开始向微软的数据中心供电，根据2023年5月签署的全球首个核聚变电力购买协议（PPA），微软将获得最高50兆瓦的电力。Helion的第七代原型机Polaris预计将展示首个由核聚变产生的电力。该公司此前已通过原型机Trenta实现了1亿摄氏度的燃料温度，这是商用核聚变电站所需的关键温度。尽管还需要获得州政府的最终许可，Helion表示将按计划在2028年实现供电目标。此外，Helion还获得了OpenAI创始人Sam Altman的支持，并成功筹集了4.25亿美元的资金。核聚变被视为未来可持续能源的重要一步，具有几乎无限的长期潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于融合能源项目的可行性、时机及其背景的讨论。

不同观点：
• **captain_coffee** 对项目可行性高度怀疑，认为报道遗漏了关键细节，特别是实际工作中的融合反应堆设计，并质疑2028年实现供电目标的可能性。
• **vessenes** 对华盛顿州资助核能项目表示惊讶，但认为在已有水电资源的基础上增加核能和基础设施可能是一个"多多益善"的策略，并设想Wenatchee未来可能成为数据中心和电力枢纽。
• **Havoc** 引用了维基百科的数据，指出融合效率正在提高，特别是2025年的最高增益Q=4.13，显示出技术的进展。
• **pfdietz** 反对一味怀疑，认为该项目有其独特的创新之处，并以SpaceX为例，建议大家在发表意见前应先了解更多细节。
• **ck2** 提供了一个PBS Space Time的视频链接，暗示这些视频可以为理解融合能源提供有价值的背景知识。
• **trhway** 提到AI数据中心对电力的巨大需求使得融合能源的时机正好，并回顾了过去类似的高风险高投资项目（如Rotary Rocket），暗示风险资本家可能看到了类似的潜力。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于融合能源项目的可行性和实际供电时间表，尤其是**captain_coffee**的怀疑与其他如**pfdietz**和**Havoc**对技术进展的乐观态度形成对比。
• **vessenes** 和 **trhway** 提到了项目背景中的市场需求和技术投资历史，为讨论提供了更广泛的视角。
• **ck2** 提供的视频链接为深入理解讨论的技术细节提供了资源支持。

总结来看，讨论主要围绕项目的可行性、时机以及技术进展，同时夹杂着对风险资本和市场需求的分析。

44745067.article_content:
Helion says reactor could deliver power to data centres by 2028
Helion has begun work on its first fusion power plant in Chelan County in the US state of Washington. Courtesy Helion.
Microsoft-backed nuclear fusion company Helion has begun work on its first fusion power plant in Chelan County in the US state of Washington.
The Orion plant is set to deliver power to Microsoft data centres in the state by 2028, should development remain on track.
Microsoft signed what it said was the world’s first power purchase agreement (PPA) for nuclear fusion in May 2023, with the company expected to offtake up to 50 MW of capacity following a one-year ramp-up period.
Privately owned Helion, founded in 2013, has said the planned operational date for this “first of its kind” facility is significantly sooner than typical projections for deployment of commercial fusion power.
The project will connect to Washington’s primary power delivery networks, allowing it to connect to the same grid just upstream of the Microsoft data centres.
“The development of a commercial fusion power facility is a crucial step in the transition to a sustainable energy future and will not only help Microsoft to achieve its goal of being carbon negative by 2030, but will also support the development of a new clean energy source for the world,” Helion said.
According to Helion, it seventh-generation prototype, Polaris, is expected to demonstrate the first electricity produced from fusion. With its previous prototype, Trenta, Helion was the first private company to achieve a fuel temperature of 100 million degrees Celsius, which is generally considered the required operating temperature for a commercial fusion power plant.
“Today is an important day – not just for Helion, but for the entire fusion industry – as we unleash a new era of energy independence and industrial renewal,” said David Kirtley, Helion’s co-founder and chief executive officer.
Company Says It Is On Track For Delivery
“Since we founded the company, we have been completely focused on preparing fusion technology for commercialisation and getting electrons on the grid. Starting site work brings us one step closer to that vision.”
The fusion firm still needs to secure the final permits from the state government to allow for the project's energisation, but said it remains on track to deliver power by 2028.
Helion is also backed by OpenAI founder Sam Altman. In January, the company announced
the successful raise of $425m
(€371m) in a Series F round. Last year, OpenAI was reportedly in talks to purchase “vast quantities” of power from Helion.
Helion has now raised more than $1bn and has a valuation of $5.4bn, including the latest fundraising round.
Earlier this month,
Google signed a 200 MW PPA
with rival fusion firm Commonwealth Fusion Systems. The power will be supplied from Commonwealth’s inaugural ARC nuclear plant. The plant has a planned capacity of 400 MW, and is projected to deliver its first power to the Virginia grid in the early 2030s.
Unlike nuclear fission, which generates energy by splitting heavy atomic nuclei, nuclear fusion produces energy by merging light nuclei into heavier ones. If made commercially viable, fusion could offer an almost unlimited long-term energy source.

data.title: Double-slit experiment holds up when stripped to its quantum essentials
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: MIT物理学家通过精简的双缝实验证实了光的波粒二象性，这一量子特性在同一时刻无法同时观察到。实验使用两个单原子作为双缝，通过激光照射，并用高敏感度相机记录散射光的干涉图样。当尝试测量光子路径时，光的波动性消失，显示粒子特性，反之亦然。该实验源自1801年托马斯·杨的双缝实验，证明光同时具有波和粒子的性质，但无法同时展现这两种特性。爱因斯坦曾对这一量子现象持不同看法，但实验结果支持了尼尔斯·波尔的观点，验证了量子力学的基本原理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：量子力学实验及其解释，特别是双缝实验及其变种（如延迟选择量子擦除实验）的最新研究和意义。

不同观点：
• [habibur] 对“延迟选择量子擦除实验”特别感兴趣，尤其是实验中可以在光子通过狭缝并撞击探测器后，再决定测量“哪条路径”，这似乎暗示光子会“倒回去”改变历史，这种时间反向影响的解释令他感到好奇。

• [cluckindan] 认为光子以无质量的非定域波的形式传播，但在与有质量的粒子碰撞时会变得定域化。他强调电磁辐射在连续场中是连续现象，但其发射和吸收等相互作用则是离散事件（量子）。

• [gwerbret] 质疑新研究的创新性，提到双缝实验的类似分析早在30多年前就已进行，并提供了一个相关研究的链接，询问是否真的有新的突破。

• [briffid] 对文章中提到的部分测量导致部分波粒二象性丧失的观点感到困惑，质疑光子是否可以按百分比划分成波和粒子的特性。

• [moktonar] 简短地提出了一种解释，认为模拟会根据约束条件“回滚”，暗示实验结果可以通过调整模型参数来解释。

补充讨论：
• 实验的新颖性和时间反向影响的解释是讨论的核心，部分评论者（如gwerbret）质疑研究的新意，而habibur则对实验的哲学和时间影响更感兴趣。
• 对波粒二象性的理解存在争议，briffid对波和粒子的比例问题表示不解，这涉及到量子力学基础概念的解读。
• 技术性链接（如mhb提供的关于量子干涉的详细解释）为讨论提供了进一步的科学背景，但未直接参与争议。

争议焦点：
• 新研究的创新性及其在量子力学基础理论中的意义。
• 波粒二象性的具体解释，尤其是如何理解部分测量对波和粒子特性的影响。

MIT physicists have performed an idealized version of one of the most famous experiments in quantum physics. Their findings demonstrate, with atomic-level precision, the dual yet evasive nature of light. They also happen to confirm that Albert Einstein was wrong about this particular quantum scenario.
The experiment in question is the
double-slit experiment
, which was first performed in 1801 by the British scholar Thomas Young to show how light behaves as a wave. Today, with the formulation of quantum mechanics, the double-slit experiment is now known for its surprisingly simple demonstration of a head-scratching reality: that light exists as both a particle and a wave. Stranger still, this duality cannot be simultaneously observed. Seeing light in the form of particles instantly obscures its wave-like nature, and vice versa.
The original experiment involved shining a beam of light through two parallel slits in a screen and observing the pattern that formed on a second, faraway screen. One might expect to see two overlapping spots of light, which would imply that light exists as particles, a.k.a. photons, like paintballs that follow a direct path. But instead, the light produces alternating bright and dark stripes on the screen, in an interference pattern similar to what happens when two ripples in a pond meet. This suggests light behaves as a wave. Even weirder, when one tries to measure which slit the light is traveling through, the light suddenly behaves as particles and the interference pattern disappears.
The double-slit experiment is taught today in most high school physics classes as a simple way to illustrate the fundamental principle of quantum mechanics: that all physical objects, including light, are simultaneously particles and waves.
Nearly a century ago, the experiment was at the center of a friendly debate between physicists Albert Einstein and Niels Bohr. In 1927, Einstein argued that a photon particle should pass through just one of the two slits and in the process generate a slight force on that slit, like a bird rustling a leaf as it flies by. He proposed that one could detect such a force while also observing an interference pattern, thereby catching light’s particle and wave nature at the same time. In response, Bohr applied the quantum mechanical uncertainty principle and showed that the detection of the photon’s path would wash out the interference pattern.

data.author: tiarafawn

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：各国农业补贴政策及其影响，以及农业发展与人口增长之间的关系

不同观点：
• **dinkblam 的观点**：澳大利亚的农业补贴非常低，其他国家应该效仿澳大利亚的做法。然而，dinkblam 认为其他国家不太可能采取类似政策。这暗示了对农业补贴过高的不满以及对澳大利亚模式的认可，但也表达了对全球政策改变的悲观态度。

• **cadamsdotcom 的观点**：支持反保护主义的立场，认为降低农业补贴是积极的一步。该评论简单明了，直接赞成减少农业保护主义措施，与 dinkblam 的观点有一定呼应。

• **skywal_l 的观点**：引用诺曼·布劳格（Norman Borlaug）的言论，强调绿色革命为人类争取了时间，但同时也指出人口增长的威胁。如果不能控制人口增长，绿色革命带来的粮食增产可能只是暂时的成功。这引出了一个长期的可持续发展问题，涉及到农业发展与人口控制之间的平衡。

补充讨论：
• **skywal_l** 的评论引用了诺贝尔奖演讲，提出了一个更深远的视角，即粮食生产技术的进步只是解决了短期问题，长期来看，人口增长可能会抵消这些技术带来的好处。这与 **dinkblam** 和 **cadamsdotcom** 更关注政策和经济层面的讨论形成对比，增加了对生态和人口因素的考量。

• 争议的焦点可能在于如何平衡农业补贴政策和自由市场之间的关系，以及如何在农业技术进步的同时应对人口增长带来的压力。这些讨论反映了不同观点持有者对全球农业和经济政策的不同优先级和关注点。

data.title: PixiEditor 2.0 – A FOSS universal 2D graphics editor
data.author: ksymph
data.article_summary: PixiEditor 2.0是一款免费开源的通用2D图形编辑器，超越了传统的像素艺术编辑器。它支持光栅和矢量图形、动画以及程序化效果，具有高度可配置的渲染管道，适用于各种工作流程。新版本引入了节点图功能，允许用户通过连接节点创建复杂效果，甚至支持创建整个工作区。此外，PixiEditor 2.0还支持像素艺术和帧动画，并计划未来添加关键帧和矢量动画功能。尽管该软件独立且开源，但为了支持项目持续发展，开发团队成立了Pixi Labs公司，计划通过销售付费扩展和资源来获取资金。

PixiEditor 2.0 - a FOSS Universal 2D Graphics Editor is here!
Krzysztof Krysiński
July 30, 2025
pixieditor
v2
launch
July 30, 2025
What is PixiEditor?
Up until today, PixiEditor was known as a pixel-art editor. Version 2.0 is much more than that. It’s a Universal 2D Editor - a brand new category.
It’s not yet another Photoshop alternative. We take the word “Universal” much more seriously. We built an extremely configurable raster/vector render pipeline, which you can adjust for any workflow you can think of.
Our goal is to build a free and open source editor that can handle all of 2D graphics
Raster
Vector,
Animations,
Procedural (VFX, effects, non-desctuctive editing)
What can it do?
Need to create a thumbnail for your YouTube video? Done. Edit SVG files? Easy. Create a pixel-art animation spritesheet? You bet.
Or maybe you have a special workflow that requires complex setup? PixiEditor can help you with most demanding needs. In the most of the other image editors, you can only do as much as developers prepared. To extend its functionality you usually need to find appropriate plugin and hope it does what you want to or try finding a clever way to solve your problem.
PixiEditor’s Node Graph on the other hand, gives you full control over the rendering of your image. For example, with Node Graph only, we managed to build a 3D cube texturing workspace with live preview. And it’s just a .pixi file that you can send to anyone.
Q1 summary blog post
very well describes most of the features present in PixiEditor 2.0. But in short:
Toolsets for any scenario
Switch between Painting, Pixel-art and Vector toolsets. Mix vectors and raster graphics in one file.
Vectors
PixiEditor natively supports editing vectors in High DPI, meaning you can edit low-res documents and combine it with vectors that will rendered crisp on the same canvas.
All vectors are non-destructive, they are preserved on separate layers and can be edited anytime.
It includes tools such as:
Path tool: Create Bézier Curves and Polygons
Line, Ellipse and Rectangle
Text
It’s far from end of the list, vectors and vector layers are very powerful in combination with
Node Graph
Node Graph
The Node Graph is one of PixiEditor’s most powerful features. It allows for creating effects previously only possible with specialized software such as game engines.
With classic layers + tools experience you can do very much, but with node graph, you can make almost anything. I’m not joking, it’s just a matter of time until someone runs Doom in it.
Basic overview
By connecting nodes you can make complex effects using simple rules. Every layer is a node and it can be connected to other nodes.
Procedurally Generated Islands with seasons animation
Fully procedural fire
Node Workspaces
To solve the issue of constant need of reattaching nodes to see their effect, we’ve implemented a special node called “Preview” which creates a custom output that can be toggled in the viewport settings
In the video above, there’s only one file that has a graph with multiple outputs. By creating 3 viewports for the same image, you can preview all the outputs at once.
This is a very powerful feature that allows you to create entire workspaces. We’ve made a
reusable pixel art case study
to demonstrate its use.
Animations
One of the most requested features in PixiEditor 1.0 was frame by frame animations, and we’ve finally delivered.
But that’s not the end, except classic cels you can utilize node graph to create procedural animations.
You can render them as a video (gif, mp4) or export to spritesheet for your games.
One missing piece of the puzzle is key frame animations and vector animations, but that’s coming later after 2.0 release.
Pixel Art Toolset
You can create pixel arts with dedicated tools, such as:
Brush with pixel-perfect option
Transform (scale, move, skew, rotate, perspective) selection and layers
Non-destructive, pixel-perfect text tool
Interested?
Make sure to read
Q1 summary blog post
for feature details
Pixi Labs and Founder’s Pack
One of the big changes that happened over past few months is the birth of Pixi Labs Sp. z o.o. - we’ve established a legal entity for PixiEditor related stuff.
But don’t worry, PixiEditor is still independent, free and open-source. We are not going to change that. However there are a lot of challenges when it comes to building open-source projects. The biggest is funding.
Over 1 year ago I left my job to finally develop PixiEditor full time. I want to keep it that way. I deeply believe in open-source and its importance in the world. Unfortunately we don’t live in a utopia and
I need to start earning money, both to buy myself food, keep PixiEditor infrastructure alive and ideally, hire other PixiEditor contributors.
How are we planning to earn money?
The deal is simple. We’ll be maintaining and developing PixiEditor for free and in the meantime we will create useful paid extensions and assets that you’ll be able to buy.
It’s a win-win.
Founder

data.title: Linear Types for Programmers (2023)
data.author: marvinborner
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了线性类型在类型理论中的应用，源自Jean-Yves Girard提出的线性逻辑。线性逻辑有四大主要操作符：独立值对（A ⊗ B）、选择（A ⊻ B）、消费者选择（A & B）和相互依赖值对（A ⅋ B）。线性类型确保每个值只能使用一次，这种特性在编程中可用于模拟资源消耗、状态变化和协议执行等场景。例如，投币购买物品后不能再用同一硬币，或文件关闭后不能再写入。线性类型还可应用于内存管理和并发编程，避免垃圾回收和死锁问题。通过这些应用，线性类型在函数式和命令式语言之间架起桥梁，使程序更高效和安全。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程语言中线性类型（Linear Types）的支持和相关语言的讨论

不同观点：
• [melodyogonna] 指出 Mojo 语言当前已经对线性类型提供了一些支持，但因为类型系统的机制尚未完善，完整的支持还在计划中。他提供了一个提案链接，详细介绍了该计划。

• [renox] 提到了 Austral 语言，它也支持线性类型，并提供了一个网站链接和相关教程，不过并未明确说明该语言的当前发展状态。

• [jnpnj] 提出一个问题，询问幻影类型（phantom types）和类型状态（typestates）是否是线性类型的子集或类似概念，暗示了对线性类型定义和分类的探讨需求。

补充讨论：
• [scythmic_waves] 偏离主题地表达了对网站设计的赞赏，未涉及线性类型的技术讨论。

争议焦点：
• 线性类型的具体定义和分类是讨论中的潜在争议点，尤其是幻影类型和类型状态是否属于线性类型或其相关概念，这引发了进一步澄清的需求。

总结：
讨论围绕几种编程语言对线性类型的支持展开，包括 Mojo 和 Austral，并引发了对线性类型及其相关概念（如幻影类型和类型状态）的定义和分类的思考。

Introduction

L
inear types are an application to type theory of the discipline of
linear logic
, first described by Jean-Yves Girard
(
Girard, 1987
).
Since its inception it has led to many fruitful discoveries in
computer science.  In this article I hope to explain why it is so
interesting, as well as relate it to concrete tools and practices
available to programmers today.
T
here are four main operators in linear logic:
\(A â B\), read
A times B
, represents an independent pair of
values that may be used in any order, similar to the
struct
in a
language like Rust;
\(A â B\), read
A plus B
, represents either an
A
or a
B
,
and the consumer must be prepared for either possibility, similar to
the
enum
in a language like Rust;
\(A \operatorname{\&} B\), read
A with B
, is either an
A
or a
B
, and the consumer gets to choose which one;
\(A \operatorname{â
} B\), read
A par B
, is an interdependent
pair of values presented in an order chosen by the producer, and the
consumer must be prepared to respond to them in any order.
A
simple form of linear types (specifically
MLL
, the fragment of
linear logic without the additive/âchoiceâ operators â and &) can be
encoded as a programming language in which each value can be used, and
must be used, exactly once, and popularized by Henry Baker in a series
of articles about applying them to remove garbage collection from
Lisp.
Henry Baker is a prominent Lisp hacker and one of the original creators of the Lisp Machine, which is sometimes considered to have lost to the C-based UNIX machines due to the long and unpredictable âpauseâ required for garbage collection on the relatively slow hardware of the time.
This is the form usually seen
in programming languages.  For example, a
Î»-calculus
term of type \(A \multimap B\) is
a function that exactly consumes one \(A\) and produces one
\(B\) â encoding a proof of the linear logic proposition
\(A^\bot \operatorname{â
} B\).
Applications
Â§
B
y employing linear types, the programmer can model systems in which
using something changes its type.  A common example involves a âcostâ:
if I have a vending machine that will give me either a chocolate bar
or a packet of crisps for a dollar, I cannot simply put the dollar in
twice and get both.  Using the dollar for one item
consumes
the
dollar, and it is no longer available to get the other item.
A
more usual example in everyday programming involves objects that
have certain protocols (a sequencing of the available operations) that
must be obeyed.  For example, once a file handle has been closed, it
can no longer be written to: from the programmerâs perspective, the
file handle no longer exists.  More sophisticated changes to state,
for example an âunopenedâ file handle whose metadata can be accessed
becoming an âopenedâ file handle to/from which the programmer can
write/read data, can be modelled as âdestroyingâ the old object and
returning a new one.
A
related application is that of a network protocol.  For example, on
a stream implementing HTTP, the server might expect the client to:
open a socket
send headers
write a request body
read a response
A
ny misordering of these operations, for example writing the request
body before the headers, constitutes an error on the part of the
client programmer.
Figure 1. An HTTP request protocol.
A
nother very important example is that of memory management.  Because
arbitrary duplication of values is disallowed, it is inherent in the
structure of the code exactly how long a value must stay around, and
therefore when it is safe to reuse its memory.  This allows linear
languages, in general, to be safely executed without recourse to a
garbage collector, reference counter, or other means of tracking
memory references â an important quality in systems languages, where
unexpected garbage collection pauses are often not an option.  More
generally, linear types can be used to bridge the gap between
functional and imperative languages.  A functional program with linear
types can be realized as an imperative program; since there is no way
to observe a value twice, the memory area backing that value can be
safely reÃ¼sed, in effect mutably updating the value, without the
possibility of the program observing the change (breaking
referential
transparency
).
L
inear types also turn out to be very useful in concurrent
programming, for two reasons:
by requiring (through a sequence of consumptions and productions)
values to be used in a certain order, they allow the specification
of protocols between concurrent components;
and, even more importantly, the separation/joining of resources in â
and â
 allows the programmer to specify when sequencing
doesnât
need to be respected, while ensuring freedom from deadlocks.

data.title: A dive into open chat protocols
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了网站管理员为防止AI公司大量抓取网站数据而采用的防护措施——Anubis系统。该系统基于Hashcash的Proof-of-Work机制，通过增加大规模抓取的成本，减轻服务器负担。虽然对普通用户影响较小，但在抓取量大时会显著增加抓取难度。Anubis是一个临时解决方案，旨在为更复杂的身份验证技术争取时间。使用该系统需要启用现代JavaScript功能，某些插件如JShelter可能需要禁用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：聊天协议的选择与比较，包括安全性、用户体验、去中心化以及协议的复杂性。

不同观点：
• [palata] 认为聊天协议受网络效应影响，用户很难从像WhatsApp这样的主流平台转移到更安全的平台（如Signal）或用户体验更好的平台（如Telegram）。用户通常选择“最少努力”的方案，而不是最佳方案。即使是开源社区，也在选择聊天系统时倾向于使用Slack或Discord，而非开源解决方案。

• [weitendorf] 对Matrix的复杂性提出批评，认为其用户体验不佳，但赞赏Zulip的UX设计，尽管担忧其设计可能会让首次使用的用户感到困惑。

• [bullen] 提到使用qTox进行语音聊天，并指出让其他人意识到他们的麦克风质量差是一个挑战。同时，提供了一个简单的可扩展聊天系统的链接。

• [yaky] 分享了使用Matrix Synapse的经验，指出了其在房间复制、数据库膨胀、媒体删除和用户删除方面的问题，并比较了Element和ElementX的功能差异。

• [rascul] 提到IRCv3目前在Libera.Chat上使用，但对于不关心IRC的人来说，v3可能没有太大意义。

• [alrs] 简单表示正在运行Prosody服务器，体验积极。

• [tomjuggler] 提到正在为自己的网站编写聊天功能，并开玩笑提到希望雇佣动漫角色来保护聊天用户。

• [ZoomZoomZoom] 讨论了聊天室中的消息顺序问题，指出在桥接的Tg-to-Matrix聊天室中经常遇到消息顺序混乱的问题，导致混淆。

• [rickcarlino] 认为IRC虽然已经过时，但仍有价值，特别是在快速构建、去中心化和零摩擦访客访问方面。对于聊天使用案例，不一定需要端到端加密。

• [BrenBarn] 讨论了去中心化通信系统中的审核问题，认为审核是限制去中心化程度的主要因素。提出了一种部分或两级去中心化的可能性，以改善当前系统的垃圾信息和审核问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于聊天协议的选择是基于用户体验、安全性还是去中心化。用户通常选择最不费力的方案，而不是技术上更优的方案。
• 去中心化通信系统中的审核问题被认为是当前协议设计中的一个主要瓶颈，需要在协议中更低层次地考虑审核机制。
• 不同用户对各种聊天系统的复杂性、用户体验和功能有不同的看法和体验，反映出聊天协议选择中的多样化需求和挑战。

44738216.article_content:
Making sure you're not a bot!
Loading...
Why am I seeing this?
You are seeing this because the administrator of this website has set up
Anubis
to protect the server against the scourge of
AI companies aggressively scraping websites
. This can and does cause downtime for the websites, which makes their resources inaccessible for everyone.
Anubis is a compromise. Anubis uses a
Proof-of-Work
scheme in the vein of
Hashcash
, a proposed proof-of-work scheme for reducing email spam. The idea is that at individual scales the additional load is ignorable, but at mass scraper levels it adds up and makes scraping much more expensive.
Ultimately, this is a hack whose real purpose is to give a "good enough" placeholder solution so that more time can be spent on fingerprinting and identifying headless browsers (EG: via how they do font rendering) so that the challenge proof of work page doesn't need to be presented to users that are much more likely to be legitimate.
Please note that Anubis requires the use of modern JavaScript features that plugins like
JShelter
will disable. Please disable JShelter or other such plugins for this domain.

data.title: TclSqueak – Program in Tcl the Smalltalk Way
data.author: ofalkaed
data.article_summary: TclSqueak 是一个图形化的面向对象编程环境，专为 Tcl 语言设计，灵感来自 Smalltalk，特别是 Squeak 环境。它具有现代化的用户界面，支持实时反馈和 TclOO、XOTcl 等面向对象扩展，兼容 Tcl 8.6。其功能包括基于 SQLite 的代码库、静态类型语法检查器，以及对 Git 等版本控制系统的支持。此外，还提供了一系列视频教程，涵盖基础编程、调试、对象自省、版本控制、代码搜索与补全以及语法检查等内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对编程语言Tcl及其现代性的评价

不同观点：
• **支持Tcl的观点**：
   - **简洁高效**：doublerabbit认为Tcl是目前他觉得最“理性”的语言，能够很好地完成工作，且没有受到企业化或官僚化的影响。
   - **怀旧与实用**：doublerabbit表示，相比2000年代后的语言，Tcl让他感觉更加简洁直接，没有受到繁文缛节的束缚。

• **对现代语言的批评**：
   - **现代语言复杂且受限**：doublerabbit认为2000年代后的编程语言大多被企业文化影响，充满了不必要的复杂性（"red tape bullshite"），虽然这些语言流行，但并不符合他的编码风格。
   - **例外：Ruby**：在一定程度上，Ruby和Tcl类似，相对简洁实用，是他能接受的少数现代语言之一。

补充讨论：
• **编码风格的差异**：doublerabbit自称是一个“非正统”的程序员，暗示他的编码风格和主流开发者不同，这可能反映了对主流开发工具和语言的抗拒或不适应。
• **争议焦点**：现代编程语言是否因为企业化而变得过于复杂。这涉及到编程语言设计中的简洁性与功能性之间的平衡问题，以及开发者对这种平衡的不同偏好。

data.title: The Big Oops in type systems: This problem extends to FP as well
data.author: ksymph
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了静态类型系统，特别是函数式编程（FP）中尝试将业务逻辑直接编码到类型系统中的问题。作者指出，尽管静态类型支持者认为更强的类型系统能更准确地捕捉领域模型，从而减少测试需求，但这种做法在面对复杂的业务逻辑时往往导致问题。文章强调了技术模型与领域现实之间的区别，指出业务规则通常是情境化的、充满例外的，而传统的代数类型系统倾向于互斥分类，无法灵活应对这种复杂性。将领域语言直接映射到类型系统中会导致脆弱的结构，难以适应业务变化，最终引发昂贵的重构。文章通过Haskell代码示例展示了随着业务需求增加，类型系统如何变得复杂和难以维护。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：类型系统与动态类型系统在业务逻辑变化时的适应性及维护成本

不同观点：
• epolanski认为，业务域变化时，最昂贵的部分是测试，而不是API或类型，并质疑重构的实际成本。
• seanwilson强调，类型系统能在编译阶段捕捉错误，减少运行时错误，而动态类型语言则依赖测试套件，这增加了维护负担。
• fcantournet指出，复杂逻辑必然导致复杂类型系统，这是类型系统在确保逻辑一致性中的正常表现。
• jayd16认为，无论是否使用静态类型，业务规则的迁移和重构同样困难，单元测试在两种情况下都能有效捕捉错误。
• sirwhinesalot提倡使用关系模型和数据库来处理业务域变化，认为主流语言在这方面表现不佳，Clojure的解决方案相对优越。
• agentultra基于Haskell的经验，认为高级类型系统不会对业务逻辑变化造成不灵活，并建议深入了解编译器和语言。
• b_e_n_t_o_n提出，将更多责任推给类型系统类似于使用一种更高阶的语言，可能导致错误转移而非消除，倾向于数据导向的编程方式。
• dang提供相关讨论链接，涉及OOP的长期问题。
• elbear认为，不喜欢编译器的人往往缺乏耐心去学习如何在语言中表达解决方案。
• jact强调模块化和抽象类型的重要性，认为良好的设计能减少类型变化对系统其他部分的影响。
• moomin指出，FP开发者欢迎类型系统在变化中的作用，相比动态类型语言，这能更早发现问题。
• hackyhacky质疑Clojure中通过代码而非类型来表达业务规则的有效性。
• fellowniusmonk从哲学角度看待类型，认为复杂类型是抽象工具而非现实反映。
• jiggawatts描述了在大规模系统中使用事件日志和松散耦合的订阅者模式，以避免状态爆炸问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于静态类型系统与动态类型系统在应对业务逻辑变化时的优劣。
• 一些人认为类型系统能在编译时捕捉错误，减少维护负担；另一些人则认为复杂的类型系统本身会带来额外复杂性。
• 讨论中还涉及到模块化设计、关系模型和事件驱动架构在处理业务规则变化中的应用和优势。
• 总体上，参与者对类型系统的价值和适用场景存在不同看法，取决于具体开发背景和经验。

44749387.article_content:
The Big Oops in Type Systems: This Problem Extends to FP as Well
Building on Casey Muratori's critique (
youtube
) of "compile time hierarchies that match the domain model," this problem extends beyond OOP to encompass a broader pattern in static type systems, particularly functional programming approaches that attempt to "make illegal states unrepresentable."
Type systems are often ranked in a "correctness hierarchy", with Idris/Haskell at the top, Java/C# in the middle, Python/JavaScript at the bottom. Static type proponents argue that better type systems can capture domain models more accurately, reducing the need for tests by proving certain software properties impossible.
The experiment of encoding complex business domains directly into mathematical type constructs has shown mixed results, succeeding in some areas while struggling with the inherent messiness of business logic. While functional programming concepts have spread to other languages, they've largely abandoned the rigid philosophy that defines languages like Haskell.
Technical Models vs. Domain Reality
There's a critical distinction between
technical understanding
(how data is processed) and
domain presentation
(how data is conceptualized within the problem domain).
Data processing works best when mapped onto "simpler" reasoning models (à la Rich Hickey's "simple not easy") and then transformed. But domain presentation must accommodate legacy and entrenched domain understanding that evolves with business requirements.
The trap is that both OOP hierarchies and FP "make illegal states unrepresentable" create
premature crystallization
of domain understanding into rigid technical models. When domains evolve (and they always do), this coupling demands expensive refactoring.
It's fascinating that an industry that learned the pitfalls of premature optimization and tight coupling has convinced itself that encoding domains into type systems is beneficial—despite creating these very same problems.
The Categorical Mismatch
Here's the thing nobody talks about: domain experts think in workflows, exceptions, and contextual rules. They'll tell you things like "normally we validate the credit card first, but if it's a returning customer and the amount is under $50, we can process it immediately" or "a shipment is 'pending' until it leaves the warehouse, except for digital goods which are 'delivered' instantly, unless there's a compliance hold."
Traditional algebraic type systems encourage exhaustive, mutually exclusive categories, though modern approaches like row types and effect systems offer more flexibility:
data
PaymentStatus
=
Pending
|
Validated
|
Failed
|
Completed
data
ShipmentStatus
=
Created
|
InTransit
|
Delivered
|
Returned
But business domains are messy, contextual, and full of overlapping states that depend on multiple factors simultaneously. Consider healthcare: patient status isn't just 'active' or 'discharged'—it depends on insurance authorization, bed availability, treatment protocols, and family preferences. In finance, a 'trade' might be pending, executed, settled, or failed, but also partially filled, awaiting counter-party confirmation, under regulatory review, or in dispute resolution.
The "ubiquitous language" from Domain-Driven Design tries to bridge this gap, but encoding domain language directly into types creates brittle mappings that satisfy nobody. Domain experts can't recognize their mental models in rigid algebraic structures, and developers get trapped maintaining complex type hierarchies that resist change.
When the business inevitably adds "VIP customers can modify orders after payment if the change is under $20," watch what happens to your beautiful type system.
In raw Haskell, you might start with clean sum types:
-- Starting simple and clean
data
PaymentStatus
=
Pending
|
Completed
|
Failed
data
Order
=
Order
{
status
::
PaymentStatus
,
customer
::
Customer
}
The new requirement forces you to encode every state combination. You end up with something like:
-- First attempt at handling the VIP modification rule
data
PaymentStatus
=
Pending
|
Completed
CompletedState
|
Failed
FailureReason
data
CompletedState
=
CompletedState
{ canModify ::
Bool
-- Based on customer type and amount
, maxModificationAmount ::
Maybe
Decimal
, customerType ::
CustomerType
, itemType ::
ItemType
}
data
CustomerType
=
Standard
|
VIP
|
Enterprise
data
ItemType
=
Physical
|
Digital
|
Service
But wait—digital goods have instant delivery, enterprise customers need approval workflows, and seasonal promotions affect modification rules. Soon you're maintaining a baroque hierarchy:
-- The inevitable complexity explosion
data
PaymentStatus
=
Pending
PendingState
|
Completed
CompletedState
|
Failed
FailureReason
|
PartiallyCompleted
PartialState
CompletedState
-- New business requirement
|
PendingApproval
ApprovalWorkflow
CompletedState
-- Enterprise customers
data
CompletedState
=
CompletedState
{ canModify ::
Bool
, maxModificationAmount ::
Maybe
Deci

data.title: Write "Freehold" Software
data.author: rjinman
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于"freehold软件"（完全所有权软件）与"leasehold软件"（租赁权软件）概念的讨论，以及软件所有权与订阅模式的争议。

不同观点：
• tpoacher支持使用"freehold软件"和"leasehold软件"的术语区分，认为这样能更清晰地传达软件所有权的区别。他以英国房产的"freehold"和"leasehold"为例，说明租赁权软件有诸多限制，类似于房产租赁中的限制和到期问题。
• ktallett同意"freehold"原则，但质疑如何让更多软件采用这种模式，指出目前成功的例子（如Goodnotes和Affinity设计应用）较少。他还提到，现代社会中，许多人不愿意为软件支付高昂的前期费用，导致订阅模式更受欢迎。
• throwpoaster认为传统软件商业模式存在成本与收入配对的问题，特别是对于需要持续服务器支持的软件。订阅模式解决了这一问题，因为可以持续获得收入来支付后续成本。
• bee_rider指出游戏软件在所有权模式上取得了一些进展，但对大多数人来说并不重要。他认为工作软件应该可以在本地运行，无需许可证服务器。同时，他质疑专有"freehold"软件的可行性，建议开源可能是更好的选择。
• tenacious_tuna对"freehold软件"的概念感兴趣，但认为作者引用ChatGPT定义自己写的术语有些不妥。他还提到ChatGPT和其他托管LLM是"freehold软件"的反面例子。
• Havoc表示对自托管感兴趣，认为适度的遥测技术（可选择退出）是可以接受的，有助于开发者了解软件的使用情况。
• Paradigm2020认为当前的"freehold"类别过于 restrictive，排除了某些优秀的游戏。他以Polytopia为例，指出微交易并不一定意味着不是"freehold"软件。
• idle_zealot认为作者所寻找的术语是Freeware、Shareware或FOSS，指出如果没有源代码的访问权，就无法真正拥有软件。
• acuozzo开玩笑地说自己来自Freehold, NJ，是否意味着他写的软件自动成为"Freehold2x"。
• layer8以幽默的方式质疑"freehold软件"是否意味着"hold my beer"（承担后果）。

补充讨论：
• 关于软件所有权与订阅模式的争议焦点在于，订阅模式提供了持续的收入流以支持软件维护和更新，但同时也限制了用户对软件的完全所有权和控制权。
• 开源软件被多次提到作为一种解决方案，可以填补专有软件在所有权和自由度方面的不足，但同时也面临商业模式的挑战。
• 讨论中还涉及了具体例子（如Goodnotes、Affinity设计应用、Polytopia）以及术语定义的准确性问题。

• idle_zealot认为作者所寻找的术语是Freeware、Shareware或FOSS，指出如果没有源代码的访问权，就无法真正拥有软件。
• acuozzo开玩笑地说自己来自Freehold, NJ，是否意味着他写的软件自动成为"Freehold2x"。
• layer8以幽默的方式质疑"freehold软件"是否意味着"hold my beer"（承担后果）。

补充讨论：
• 关于软件所有权与订阅模式的争议焦点在于，订阅模式提供了持续的收入流以支持软件维护和更新，但同时也限制了用户对软件的完全所有权和控制权。
• 开源软件被多次提到作为一种解决方案，可以填补专有软件在所有权和自由度方面的不足，但同时也面临商业模式的挑战。
• 讨论中还涉及了具体例子（如Goodnotes、Affinity设计应用、Polytopia）以及术语定义的准确性问题。

• **[观点二：市场表现正常，夸大其词]**  
  *darth_avocado* 反驳“房屋销售不佳”的说法，认为这种叙述被夸大。他指出，供应月份同比保持稳定，独栋房屋和公寓的中位数销售天数仅略微增加。同时，售出的房屋数量同比增加，虽然待售房屋数量同比增加15%，但这并不能证明房屋难以出售。他还质疑了一些文章为吸引点击而夸大其词的性质，提供了Redfin的数据支持自己的论点。

  *01HNNWZ0MV43FF* 提出，实施土地价值税可以解决房屋供应问题，通过减少对空置土地和汽车经销店的补贴，从而促进住房建设。

  *cyanydeez* 认为，当前的房地产市场是由企业所有权人为造成的，市场失真源于企业对市场的控制。他主张停止对市场的过度测量，认为这样可以消除企业对市场的扭曲影响。

• 数据可靠性和解读：*darth_avocado* 强调数据的重要性，并引用Redfin数据来支持自己的观点，反驳那些认为市场低迷的说法。

争议焦点：房屋销售是否真的不佳，以及造成市场现状的主要原因是什么。

data.title: Introduction to Unikernel: Building, deploying lightweight, secure applications
data.author: eyberg
data.article_summary:
本文主要介绍了一种名为unikernel的专用应用环境，其类似于租用的私人别墅，提供独占资源，不与其他应用共享。Unikernel是一种紧凑、单应用的虚拟机，能提升速度、效率和安全性。传统操作系统如Linux和Windows设计为同时运行多个应用，导致不必要的资源消耗。Unikernel通过将应用与操作系统合并为单一可执行映像，减少了这些开销，从而加快启动时间，降低内存消耗，并提升安全性。

本文还比较了两种主要的unikernel类型：Nanos和Unikraft。Nanos允许创建可在多种云服务上运行的映像，而Unikraft依赖其专用的云结构以获得更好性能。最后，文章提供了创建和部署Nanos unikernel的步骤指南。通过使用OPS工具，用户可以简化映像和实例的创建过程。

44757249.article_content:
Have you ever wondered what it would be like to have everything in the world just for yourself — where every resource and every service is just for you? Imagine you have rented a private villa on a small, quiet island. Everything in the villa — the rooms, the pool, and the beach — is just for you. No other guests can use anything there, and the staff are there just for you. Isn’t that exciting? I’m sure it is!
This concept also applies to applications, which are given their own space to work in without interference from others and without sharing resources. Any application could thrive in such an environment. So, the question is: “Does such an application environment exist?”
Enter unikernels — a unique application environment that can provide an exclusive environment just like your private villa. They are compact, single-application virtual machines, boosting speed, efficiency, and security.
In this article, we will take a closer look at what unikernels are, explore the different types of unikernels, discuss their benefits and limitations, and learn how to create and deploy a simple Nanos application (a type of unikernel) on AWS.
What is a Unikernel and why do we need it?
Before we look at unikernels, let us first understand why we need something like unikernels in the first place, and examine the limitations of current operating systems like Linux and Windows that lead us to look for alternatives.
Traditional operating systems are designed to run multiple applications simultaneously, which requires careful resource management to ensure smooth operation. The operating system kernel also performs numerous background tasks via memory management, process scheduling, disk I/O and peripheral management. However, our backend applications often do not need these functions, and yet the kernel consumes a lot of memory and CPU power to support them.
The solution to the above problem is simple: if the operating system causes too much overhead, why not let the user-space program take control of the hardware directly? This way, the application essentially becomes part of the kernel, accesses the hardware with fewer obstacles and significantly reduces the overhead of the operating system.
This is exactly the goal of unikernels — fine-tuning for specific tasks. They are lightweight, specialized virtual machines designed to run a single application, making the system smaller, faster and more secure. This unique form of virtualization merges the application and operating system into a single executable image, eliminating the need for the extensive features and services of traditional operating systems.
This specialization makes the system simpler and reduces resource consumption. It only contains the essential components required for the respective application and is, therefore, much smaller than conventional operating systems. This lean design leads to faster boot times and lower memory consumption. In addition, the smaller attack surface of unikernels also improves security.
Since it is executed as a single process, there is no overhead from context switching between multiple processes, resulting in faster execution and lower latency. Once compiled, unikernels can be run on local devices on Linux with QEMU and even on various hypervisors such as Xen, KVM, Nitro System and ESXi.
These hypervisors handle the interaction with the underlying hardware, allowing unikernels to benefit from virtualization without the overhead of a full operating system. The following block diagram will help you to better understand and visualize the whole thing.
Types of Unikernel
Recently, we reached out to several unikernel teams for one of our projects, but only received a few responses. After investigating some of the unikernels, we realized that only two — Nanos and Unikraft — are on the path to stability. Although conceptually both have the same basic principle, they have their own methods for deploying unikernel images and instances.
The main differences between the two unikernels are listed in the table below. However, one of the main differences between Unikraft and Nanos is that Unikraft relies more on its own cloud structure called Unikraft Cloud (which is ultimately based on a bare metal instance) for better performance, while Nanos offers the ability to create its own image that can run on all instance types on all cloud providers supported by Nanos.
Building Nanos unikernel (step-by-step instructions)
We have mentioned about Unikraft, but let’s leave that aside for now and concentrate on nanos.
Creating a Nanos unikernel involves several steps, from setting up the environment to deploying the final image and instance. In addition, Nanos uses an operational tool called OPS that streamlines various tasks, such as image and instance creation.

data.title: The Garlic Bread Hack
data.author: kenshi
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种替代传统大蒜面包或披萨的健康零食：空气爆米花配自制大蒜黄油和牛至。作者通过实验发现，人们的食欲往往源于对味道的记忆，而非特定的食物本身。这种爆米花在几分钟内制作完成，热量较低，但能提供相似的满足感。关键在于牛至等调料，使它不仅健康，还具有诱人的风味。作者建议读者尝试这种替代品，并根据个人口味和营养目标调整配方，核心在于能否满足食欲。

44736428.article_content:
What if the thing you're craving isn't actually what you need?
Last night at a Hacker News meetup, I shared something I'd been experimenting with. When I want garlic bread (or pizza), I make this instead:
Air-popped popcorn
Fresh garlic butter (real butter, fresh garlic, sizzled together)
A sprinkle of oregano
Three ingredients. 5 mins cooking time. A delicious, filling snack that hits the spot.
Here's what I've learned: our cravings are often about flavor memories, not the delivery system.
You don't actually want 300 calories of refined flour. You want that hit of garlic and herbs. You want something warm and savory that feels indulgent.
The popcorn delivers. The whole bowl has fewer calories than two slices of garlic bread, but somehow hits the same satisfaction buttons. It's the oregano that seals the deal - suddenly you're not eating "diet food," you're eating something that tastes great and is associated with fun.
You can adjust the recipe for taste and your nutrition goals. If you are cutting back on calories,
be careful about how much butter (or other fats) you use
.
Try this tonight and let me know what you think. The real test isn't whether it's healthy (it is). It's whether it scratches the itch.

data.title: Electron beam irradiation decomposes Teflon-like fluoroplastics efficiently
data.author: westurner
data.article_summary: 日本量子科学技术研究机构的团队开发了一种高效回收聚四氟乙烯（PTFE，俗称特氟隆）的方法。传统的分解方法需要极高温度（600-1000°C）和大量能量，而该团队通过电子束（EB）照射结合加热，在370°C下实现了PTFE的完全分解。这种方法将所需能量减少了50%，并将塑料转化为气态产物，如含氟氧化物和全氟烷烃，这些气体可作为化学工业的原料再利用。该技术有望实现特氟隆的大规模、可持续回收，具有商业应用潜力。研究成果发表在《Radiation Physics and Chemistry》期刊上。

Plastics like PTFE, commonly known as Teflon, are durable, yet difficult to decompose. Moreover, traditional methods for decomposing PTFE require extremely high temperatures and massive energy inputs. Now, however, researchers from Japan have put forth a promising method for enhancing the energy efficiency of PTFE recycling. Credit: Dr. Akira Idesaki from National Institutes for Quantum Science and Technology, Japan
Plastics like Teflon are famously durable—and infamously difficult to recycle. But a breakthrough from researchers at the National Institutes for Quantum Science and Technology (QST) may offer a powerful new solution.
The team, led by Senior Principal Researcher Dr. Akira Idesaki, has developed a technique using
electron beam
(EB) irradiation to break down polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) into gaseous products, effectively transforming a solid, heat-resistant fluoropolymer into useful chemical components. Their results are
published
in the journal
Radiation Physics and Chemistry
.
"By applying heat during irradiation, we were able to reduce the energy required to decompose PTFE by 50% compared to traditional methods," said Dr. Idesaki. "This makes large-scale recycling of fluoropolymers much more viable."
PTFE—best known by the trade name Teflon—is widely used in electronics, medical devices, and nonstick cookware. Its resistance to heat and chemicals comes from its strong carbon-fluorine bonds, which also make it a member of the environmentally persistent family of substances known as PFAS, which are informally called "forever chemicals."
Traditional methods for decomposing PTFE, such as pyrolysis, require extremely
high temperatures
(600-1,000 °C) and massive energy input. The QST team demonstrated that heating PTFE to 370 °C and irradiating it with an EB in the air allowed them to convert 100% of the plastic into gas.
Get free science updates with Science X Daily and Weekly Newsletters —
subscribe now
to customize your preferences!
Gases from solids: The chemistry of breakdown
The key to the method is combining heat with radiation. When PTFE powder was irradiated with a dose of 5 MGy at 30 °C, only 10% decomposed. But at 270 °C, that number rose to 86%. At 370 °C, full decomposition was achieved.
The main gases released during the process were oxidized fluorocarbons—
chemical compounds
that contain both fluorine and oxygen, and perfluoroalkanes—compounds containing fluorine and carbon. The research team identified them using
gas chromatography
and mass spectrometry. These gases could be collected and reused as
raw materials
in chemical industries, helping to support a more sustainable, circular use of resources.
Structural transformation and crystallinity
The researchers also found that heating PTFE during EB irradiation caused changes in its internal structure. The small crystal units inside the material became larger, which suggests that the material underwent a reorganization. Infrared and X-ray analysis showed that most of the oxidized chemicals were removed, meaning the PTFE was efficiently broken down into gas.
"High-temperature irradiation not only enhances decomposition but also changes the internal structure of PTFE," noted the first-author Dr. Hao Yu, a researcher at QST. "This helps explain why the process becomes more energy-efficient as the temperature rises."
Toward industrial application
Based on their data, the researchers estimate that this new approach could cut the energy cost of PTFE recycling from approximately 2.8–4 MWh per ton—typical for pyrolysis (high temperature)—by 50% using EB irradiation. This level of efficiency could make it commercially attractive for industries that generate PTFE waste.
"We hope this technology will contribute to the safer, cleaner, and more cost-effective recycling of high-performance plastics," said co-author Dr. Yasunari Maekawa, who led the research project.

Hao Yu et al, Effects of temperature on the decomposition of PTFE induced by electron beam irradiation,
Radiation Physics and Chemistry
(2025).

data.title: What's so bad about nicotine?
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了2025年尼古丁产品的复杂性。传统上，尼古丁因与吸烟相关的健康风险而被视为有害，但近年来不含烟草的尼古丁替代品（如电子烟和尼古丁袋）变得流行。这些产品被认为比传统香烟危害小，美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）也批准了某些品牌的销售。然而，尽管广告宣称尼古丁有放松和提升认知功能的作用，专家对其健康影响的看法不一。一些研究显示尼古丁可能对身体有潜在风险，如加速肿瘤生长和引发心血管问题。此外，尼古丁的成瘾性极强，戒除难度堪比海洛因。因此，虽然新型尼古丁产品相对 safer，但其长期影响仍不明确，公众健康专家对此持不同意见。

For the better part of the past century, the case against nicotine was simple: Smoking a cigarette might feel nice, but it will eventually kill you. Nearly one in five deaths in the United States is caused by complications from cigarette smoke. Chewing tobacco is less dangerous, but still deadly: It has long been associated with head and neck cancers.
But in 2025, nicotine isn’t so straightforward. Smoking is so deadly not because of nicotine, per se, but because of tobacco: Lighting a cigarette burns tobacco, releasing nicotine into the body. Chewing tobacco entails gnawing on actual tobacco leaves. Nowadays, it’s easier than ever to get a nicotine buzz without any tobacco at all: Just puff on a vape or pop a tiny nicotine pouch between your teeth and upper lip. These cigarette alternatives have been around for a while, but only recently have they gone fully mainstream. In January, the FDA officially sanctioned the sale of Zyn, among the most recognizable nicotine-pouch brands. In the past three months alone, Philip Morris International, which makes Zyn, shipped 190 million cans of the stuff to stores. And last month, the agency reversed a prior ruling and authorized Juul e-cigarettes. These products, the FDA has concluded, “generally have lower health risks than cigarettes.”
In this nicotine boom, it’s easy to see the drug as harmless, even good for you. Ads that tout the benefits of nicotine are everywhere: Zyn, for example, has been marketed as an “office essential” that also offers “relaxation on-the-go.” Nicotine somehow feels both energizing and relaxing at the same time, kind of like the buzz of a vodka Red Bull. The drug
has been linked
to statistically significant improvements in a number of cognitive exercises. The marketing goes further: Joe Rogan has hawked Athletic Nicotine, a nicotine-pouch brand that claims the drug can serve as an “exercise performance-enhancing tool.” Tucker Carlson—who has his own brand of nicotine pouches—recently claimed that because of nicotine, he is “never sick.”
Read: The inconvenient truth about vaping
But nicotine is not a wonder drug. The cognitive improvements found in studies were modest. Bethea AnnaLouise Kleykamp, an assistant professor of psychiatry at the University of Maryland who has studied nicotine, summed it up this way: The drug “might be, if you were to subtract it from the smoke, something that could help some people,” such as those who are sleep-deprived or have a cognitive disorder like ADHD. Not exactly a ringing endorsement. Moreover, there’s still a lot we don’t know about what nicotine alone does to the body.
All of this has nicotine in a strange place. Before the advent of newer products, the field of public health was united in its stance that no one should be using cigarettes, and thus nicotine. Now the message is more muddled than ever.
Some public-health experts still suggest staying away from nicotine in and of itself. After the decades-long war against smoking, they see new products as Big Tobacco’s latest gambit to hook the public. Others make a different calculation: If the health effects of nicotine alone are less concerning than those of cigarettes, what’s so bad about an adult sucking on a Zyn? Presuming people recognize that these products “may have some health risks,” Neal Benowitz, an emeritus professor of medicine at UC San Francisco, told me, “I have no problem with that.”
Such differing views stem from the unclear health effects of cigarette alternatives. Consuming nicotine via vape or pouch is surely safer than smoking a cigarette, but that isn’t saying much. No researchers I spoke with gave nicotine an unequivocal endorsement. “I would never go so far as to say that any drug is completely safe,” Jed Rose, an emeritus professor of psychiatry at Duke University who runs a research firm that has done paid research for nicotine companies, told me. “Whether nicotine contributes in any way to other diseases associated with smoking is not as firmly resolved as people like to think.”
Rose cited a study that showed nicotine accelerated tumor growth in mice. Other experts I spoke with cited data from Sweden demonstrating that smokeless products carry some cardiovascular risks. And emerging research indicates that the components inside of vapes can leach heavy metals into the mist that users inhale, potentially exposing them to increased cancer risk. For the most part, science simply hasn’t answered the question of how bad nicotine alone is for you. Most of the studies on the bodily effects of nicotine have been completed using subjects who smoke.
For now, the clearest problem with puffing on a Juul is that nicotine remains extremely addictive, whatever form it comes in. Addiction researchers have said that nicotine is just as difficult to quit as heroin. Smokeless products might b

data.title: If You're So Smart, Why Are You So Poor?
data.author: paulpauper
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：聪明才智与财富积累之间的关系

不同观点：
• [interstice] 认为，在商业中，不择手段（being nasty）往往能带来成功，但本人选择坚持自己的道德标准，最终虽然不是特别富有，但仍为自己取得的成就感到自豪。这表明，聪明的人可能选择不滥用智力去伤害他人。
• [chistev] 表示，经常思考为何一些不如自己聪明的人更富有，并观察到聪明与财富之间似乎存在反比关系。
• [yunruse] 提出，智商测试仅能衡量模式识别和推断能力，财富的积累在满足基本需求后变得不再重要，生活的其他方面同样具有价值。
• [oh_fiddlesticks] 引用《传道书》中的经文，指出聪明、智慧和财富之间没有必然联系，时间和意外事件会影响每个人的命运。
• [ameliaquining] 对高智商人物如William James Sidis的智商估算提出质疑，强调对可验证事实的疏忽会影响文章的可信度，并指出Sidis的个人经历和社会背景对其人生有重要影响。
• [bix6] 以幽默的方式回应，未直接参与讨论。
• [h_tbob] 从基督教教义出发，认为真正聪明且虔诚的人应放弃财富，服务于上帝，并指出金钱体系基于恐惧，好人是不会愿意使用这种体系的。
• [paulpauper] 引用经济学家James Heckman的数据，指出智商对收入差异的解释力仅为1-2%，其他因素对财富积累更为重要，聪明人在通过筛选和面试时具有优势，但最终收入与智商关联不大。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及智商测试的局限性，以及智商与财富之间是否存在直接关系。
• 宗教信仰在看待财富和聪明才智方面的影响，特别是基督教教义中对财富的看法。
• 幽默和轻松的回应在讨论中提供了一种不同的视角，虽然未深入讨论主题。
• 争议的焦点在于聪明才智与财富积累之间的因果关系，以及其他因素如道德选择、个人背景和意外事件对成功的影响。

data.article_summary: 新研究发现，早期人类祖先如南方古猿阿法种（Australopithecus afarensis）和南方古猿非洲种（A. africanus）中，雄性体型显著大于雌性，差异甚至超过现代人类和部分大猩猩。这项由奥尔巴尼大学人类学家Adam D. Gordon领导的研究发表在《美国生物人类学杂志》上，采用了克服化石记录不完整限制的新方法。结果显示，早期人类祖先可能生活在雄性竞争激烈的社会系统中，这种竞争导致了性别间显著的体型差异。高性别尺寸二型性（SSD）通常与雄性间的激烈竞争及多配偶制相关，而现代人类的SSD较低，显示出不同的进化压力和社会结构。研究还表明，资源压力也可能影响雌性体型，进一步加大性别间的尺寸差异。

by Michael Parker,
